**Result (2026-05-07):** Implemented in worktree m3a/W1-migrations.  Migration 007 adds UNIQUE INDEX ux_fd_fn_lnd as fail-closed lnd-drift guard (ADR-M3-A1).  Migration 008 extends fiscal_documents.state CHECK list with 'SENDING' via a data-safe table rebuild.

Rebuild design: snapshot fiscal_documents AND document_files into non-FK holding tables, drop both, recreate fiscal_documents under the same name (no ALTER TABLE RENAME), restore rows, recreate the four attached objects, then recreate document_files with FK and restore its rows.  PRAGMA defer_foreign_keys=ON inside the sqlx-managed transaction defers self-FK (related_receipt_id) validation to COMMIT.  Two FK hazards drove this design:
  1. document_files has ON DELETE CASCADE to fiscal_documents (002).  defer_foreign_keys defers VALIDATION but not the EXECUTION of CASCADE actions, so a naive DROP TABLE fiscal_documents would silently delete every document_files row.  We snapshot document_files first.
  2. Empirical SQLite quirk (sqlite3 3.45.1, repro 2026-05-07): the standard CREATE _new / INSERT / DROP old / ALTER RENAME pattern fails at COMMIT under defer_foreign_keys=ON when a self-FK is present, even though PRAGMA foreign_key_check returns no violations mid-transaction.  Recreating fiscal_documents under the same name (no RENAME) avoids the quirk by keeping every FK reference bound to a stable table name throughout.

All four objects are recreated: the 002 non-unique ix_fd_fn_lnd (redundancy hygiene out of W1 scope), the 007 UNIQUE ux_fd_fn_lnd, ix_fd_state_pending with 'SENDING' added to its WHERE predicate, ix_fd_recon_manual, and the fd_updated_at trigger.

tasks.description:

IN_WITH_IMMEDIATE + scope), crypto/in_process.rs + transports/dps/grpc.rs + channel.rs (debug_assert! at every M2 substrate public-API entry), tests/with_immediate_no_foreign_io.rs (W5-sibling syn-based AST scanner with denylist including spawn_blocking + block_in_place literal call expressions), tests/with_immediate_runtime_guard.rs (5 §9.1 fixtures).  Bundle code+tests.

```json:metadata
{"files":["rust/prro/src/db/tx.rs","rust/prro/src/crypto/in_process.rs","rust/prro/src/transports/dps/grpc.rs","rust/prro/src/transports/dps/channel.rs","rust/prro/tests/with_immediate_no_foreign_io.rs","rust/prro/tests/with_immediate_runtime_guard.rs"],"verifyCommand":"cargo test -p prro --test with_immediate_no_foreign_io --test with_immediate_runtime_guard","acceptanceCriteria":["tokio::task_local! setup correct","debug_assert! at every M2 substrate entry","static scan catches substrate methods + spawn_blocking + block_in_place","5 §9.1 fixtures behave per spec","release build zero perf cost"]}
```

**Result (2026-05-08):** Implemented in worktree m3a/W3-with-immediate-enforcement (off rust-gateway after W1 + W4 + CI-fix + W2 merged).

Core (db/tx.rs): added `tokio::task_local! { pub(crate) static IN_WITH_IMMEDIATE: (); }` (NOT thread_local — tokio multi-threaded runtime migrates polled futures across worker threads after .await; per-task storage stays visible).  Inline helper `assert_not_in_with_immediate(method: &'static str)` with `#[inline]` debug_assert wrapping `IN_WITH_IMMEDIATE.try_with(|_| ()).is_err()` — release builds compile to no-op.  with_immediate body wraps closure in `IN_WITH_IMMEDIATE.scope((), async { let mut wt = WriteTxConn::new(&mut conn); f(&mut wt).await }).await` — the W2 inner-block lifetime hygiene preserved because the WriteTxConn borrow ends with the scope future.

11 substrate entry points instrumented (one-liner each via helper, not 11 hand-written debug_asserts): InProcessProvider::{sign_cms_detached, verify_dstu, unwrap_envelope, fetch_cert_by_ski} (4); GrpcDpsChannel::{send_chk, last_chk, ping, status_rro, info_rro} (5); DpsChannel default trait methods {by_server_fiscal_no, query_by_local_identity} (2).  cert_refresher service-layer NOT instrumented — design-precondition that crypto fetch happens BEFORE with_immediate (cert_refresher.rs:242 comment).

Static scan (tests/with_immediate_no_foreign_io.rs): syn-based AST visitor walks rust/prro/src/**/*.rs, locates every with_immediate(...) call expression, and walks the closure argument.  Three structural gates are enforced in the scan:
  1. The `with_immediate` second argument MUST be an inline `Expr::Closure` — non-inline form (`let f = move |c| ...; with_immediate(pool, f)`) is itself flagged because the body lives in `f` and the scanner cannot resolve local bindings.  Without this gate a determined caller could move forbidden code into the binding and bypass body inspection entirely.
  2. Inside the closure body, `Expr::MethodCall` with method names in the 11-substrate denylist (sign_cms_detached, verify_dstu, unwrap_envelope, fetch_cert_by_ski, send_chk, last_chk, ping, status_rro, info_rro, by_server_fiscal_no, query_by_local_identity).
  3. Inside the closure body, `Expr::Call` whose callee path's last segment is in {spawn_blocking, block_in_place} OR in the 11-substrate denylist (the latter catches UFCS / associated-function-style invocations like `CryptoProvider::fetch_cert_by_ski(&p, ...)` that would slip past a method-call-only scanner).
Detection runs on call expressions, NOT just .await paths — `let fut = provider.sign_cms_detached(...); fut.await` is caught at the call expression, closing the variable-storage hole.  Production scan over rust/prro/src/ green (no real violations); positive controls live as **synthetic snippets** parsed inline by the harness for cases 1 (direct method call), 1-saved-then-await, 1-UFCS, 3 (spawn_blocking), 3-block_in_place, and 3-non-inline-closure-bypass — we never commit a forbidden call site to source just to drive a positive test.

Runtime guard (tests/with_immediate_runtime_guard.rs): three #[tokio::test(multi_thread)] fixtures using fetch_cert_by_ski(&[], ...) — chosen because the assert at line 1 panics inside with_immediate (before the urls.is_empty() early return) but outside with_immediate the same call returns Err(CryptoError::CertFetch) without panic.  Case 2 (indirect via local_helper) panics with `foreign IO inside with_immediate: fetch_cert_by_ski`; case 4 (direct entry positive control) same panic message; case 5 (negative control outside with_immediate) returns CryptoError::CertFetch without panic.  No provider-spy / spawn_blocking_count instrumentation: structural proof 'guard is the first statement' makes tests deterministic; the panic message naming the substrate method is the assertion target.

Verified: cargo build -p prro --locked clean; cargo clippy -p prro --all-targets --no-deps -- -D warnings clean (after fixing unit-struct default + doc-list-overindentation + dead_code on Violation.file); cargo fmt -p prro -- --check clean; targeted suite (with_immediate_no_foreign_io 8/8, with_immediate_runtime_guard 3/3, tx_with_immediate_lock 3/3, transition_state_atomicity 2/2, repo_fiscal_documents_state_cas 10/10, repo_shifts 5/5) all green; full cargo test -p prro --locked 27 test files, 189 tests, 0 failed (+11 vs W2 baseline: 8 static-scan tests + 3 runtime guard tests).
